extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, policymakers, patent practitioners, and stakeholders (user community)
extracted.subtask_short: USPTO patent policy and performance review
extracted.subtask_description: An annual advisory report reviewing USPTO patent policies, goals, performance, budget, and recommending operational, quality, IT, fee, PTAB, and legislative actions to improve patent reliability, examination quality, and stakeholder transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend and/or make permanent USPTO fee-setting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Commending the President and Congress for extending: (i) the USPTO’s fee setting authority until 2026 and recommending that this fee setting authority being made permanent to ensure that the USPTO is able to recover its costs and access to all future fee collections, regardless of any government-wide sequestration or other limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: ensures USPTO can recover costs and access fee collections irrespective of sequestration or other limits; recommended permanence to provide budgetary certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceed with proposed fee adjustments (2021) with stakeholder input
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommending that the USPTO: (i) proceed with the fee adjustments it recently proposed for 2021, while taking into account stakeholder input so as to achieve reliability and certainty in U.S. patent rights and to ensure necessary and continued improvements in the USPTO’s information technology systems;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: move forward expeditiously with rulemaking while communicating to the public how additional revenue is necessary for reliability, IT improvements, timely processing, and a robust operating reserve; consider stakeholder critiques of individual adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase patent operating reserve to $747 million (~3 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manage expenditures and collections to significantly increase its operating reserve for patents to the recommended level of $747 million equivalent to at least three months of operating requirements as soon as practical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale & examples: Operating reserve critical during appropriations lapses/government shutdowns; helps sustain long-term IT initiatives through revenue fluctuations; recommended immediate goal is $747M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in and modernize USPTO information technology systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommending that the USPTO continue to invest and modernize its information technology systems to meet its goals of improving the reliability and certainty of patent rights and to support patent examiners in achieving and maintaining higher quality search and examination while helping to keep applicants’ critical technical information secure from theft by private as well as state actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific needs: upgrade/replace antiquated infrastructure, improve examiner search tools, improve public-facing reliability (reduce outages/slow access), strengthen security of applicant technical information; tie investments to measurable improvements in search/examination capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and update current patent quality metrics for public access
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommending that the USPTO: (i) maintain and update current patent quality metrics for public access so that there is full transparency regarding its quality metrics and compliance data;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: update Patent Data Visualization Center regularly (last updated FY2015 at time of report); provide full transparency on quality metrics and compliance data to the public; share data timely (not delayed until late in fiscal year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop tools/resources to enable examiners to find best, most relevant prior art early
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommending that the USPTO: (ii) develop tools and resources that will enable examiners to find and access the best, most relevant prior art at an early stage in the examination process;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples & initiatives: upgraded electronic search tools, Access to Relevant Prior Art Initiative, IP5 Collaborative Search and Examination Pilot, Diagnostic Interview Pilot; objective is to reduce issuance of claims later found unpatentable by PTAB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track investment in quality-related projects and disclose to public
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommending that the USPTO: (iii) track the investment made in terms of budget and other resources in quality-related projects for disclosure and discussion with the user community and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: identify projects expected to produce measurable results, track budgets and resources, analyze return on investment to reassure stakeholders that quality investments produce measurable improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish timeline and FY targets for meeting AIPA guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommending publication of a timeline and specific fiscal year targets for meeting the guarantees of the American Inventors Protection Act of 1999 (AIPA) to promote accountability within the USPTO, foster oversight of USPTO operations, and improve the perception of the USPTO as an efficient and fair government agency by the user community and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: define clear targets and timelines for statutorily-mandated publication/accessibility guarantees and measure performance against them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage PTAB process changes to render well-reasoned decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applauding the USPTO’s Patent Trial and Appeal Board’s (PTAB) new initiatives regarding its processes and proceedings (e.g., Claim Construction Final Rules, Comments on Motion to Amend Practice, Assignments of Judges to Panels, Formation of Precedential Opinion Panel, Trial Practice Guide Update, etc.) and requesting that the PTAB continue to look for ways to improve such processes and proceedings so as to render well-reasoned decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: continue implementing SOPs (panel assignments, opinion designations), form Precedential Opinion Panel for issues of exceptional importance, issue guidance on SAS/Aqua Products conformity; soliciting stakeholder feedback is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit stakeholder feedback and measure PTAB performance before/after changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC encourages the PTAB to continue soliciting stakeholder feedback as often as possible and seek input from parties on both sides of the patent challenge so that it can measure its performance and compare outcomes before and after the implementation of these changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: collect and analyze data to compare outcomes pre- and post-implementation of PTAB changes; solicit input from both petitioners and patent owners to measure balance and effect on patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospectively analyze whether examiners had the relevant prior art in-filed cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO should retrospectively analyze whether, during the examination phase, examiners found that particular prior art (later relied upon in PTAB proceedings). If the determination is that all of the relevant prior art was not found by or provided to the examiner, the USPTO should investigate why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: use results to close gap between issued claims and PTAB outcomes; implement investigations into search processes; inform further training/tooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define a trackable in-process quality metric for examiner exposure to relevant prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO define a trackable quality metric that provides an in-process measure of the extent to which the examiners had before them all of the relevant prior art at particular points in the examination process, such as before issuing the first office action and before an allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: metric must be trackable, tied to examination milestones (first office action, allowance), and used to monitor improvement in search coverage and examination completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage data to analyze compliance for 35 U.S.C. § 101 (subject matter eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO leverage its growing database to analyze the compliance data for rejections made under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as it continues its efforts to bring further reliability and predictability to subject matter eligibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: analyze office actions and outcomes to increase predictability; use compliance data to shape guidance and examiner training on §101.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement and expand initiatives to improve prior art searching and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the initiatives directed to improving the prior art searching conducted by examiners and the accessibility of relevant prior art to examiners at the outset of examination are collaborative, cross-functional projects within the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Diagnostic Interview Pilot (pre-search interviews), Access to Relevant Prior Art Initiative, Post Grant Outcomes Program, upgraded electronic search tools, IP5/ECS pilots; recommendation to continue and leverage cross-functional efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic Interview Pilot (pre-search interview to focus search)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Diagnostic Interview Pilot, an examiner may request a pre-search interview with the applicant to better understand the claimed invention and scope of the claims in order to formulate a more focused search strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: promotes shared responsibility between examiner and applicant for examination quality; intended to yield more focused prior art searches early in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Readiness Analysis and education on best application practices
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Application Readiness Study, the USPTO aims to assess attributes of incoming patent applications that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the patent examination process. Using that information, the USPTO can educate the public on best practices in preparing patent applications for an efficient and effective examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: identify application attributes correlated with efficient examination; develop public guidance and examiner outreach to improve application quality prior to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain security measures to protect applicant technical information
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in IT upgrades to keep applicants’ critical technical information secure from theft by private as well as state actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: security is a core justification for IT investment; protections should meet risks from both private and state threats and be part of modernization planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase transparency and frequency of publication of quality data
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO maintain and update current patent quality metrics for public access on the USPTO website so that there is full transparency to the public regarding the quality metrics and compliance data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: avoid long lags between data updates (e.g., last update FY2015); share External Quality Survey and statutory compliance data promptly and in accessible formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify return on investment for quality initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO undertake analysis to quantify the return on the significant investments the USPTO makes every year in quality initiatives, beginning with tracking the investment made in terms of budget and other resources in at least those quality-related projects expected to produce measurable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: track budget/resource allocation per project, define measurable outcomes, assess whether investments produce improvement in quality metrics and PTAB/post-grant outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure USPTO retains independent control over HR, IT, and procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing to recommend that the USPTO maintain independent control over the management and operation of its human resources, information technology and procurement functions and not expend USPTO user fees for start-up costs associated with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Enterprise Services organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal basis & guidance: statutory constraints (35 U.S.C. §42(c)(3) and 35 U.S.C. §1(a)) preclude diversion of patent user fees and require USPTO control; avoid pooling support services that are suboptimal for mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and meet pendency targets and manage filing volumes/backlogs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend publication of timeline and specific fiscal year targets for meeting statutory guarantees; monitor filing volumes and backlogs, average and absolute pendency, and prosecution options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: set measurable pendency targets (e.g., first action, total pendency), track backlog metrics, and provide prosecution option statistics to users for transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support global cooperation, work sharing, and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting the USPTO’s ongoing efforts as a leader in: (i) intellectual property policy discussions with other U.S. agencies as well as other counterpart governments and intellectual property offices; (ii) global patent work sharing programs, such as the Expanded Collaborative Search Pilots and the IP5 Patent Cooperation Treaty Collaborative Search and Examination Pilot, which aim to improve patent examination quality and efficiency; and (iii) outreach activities to bring subject matter experts to applicants around the United States in order to help applicants be better informed about ongoing international patent-related developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: support engagement with IP5, PCT systemic improvements, work sharing, Cooperative Patent Classification; leverage international pilots to improve examiner access to relevant prior art and harmonize practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and implement diversion/remediation programs for practitioner misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Applauding the USPTO for designing and implementing the Diversion Pilot Program, which is a much-needed program for practitioners whose physical, mental, or emotional health issues (including substance or alcohol abuse) or law practice management issues resulted in minor misconduct before the USPTO and allowing them the ability to rectify such misconduct through participation in the Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: supports remediation over punishment for minor misconduct due to health/practice issues; includes outreach and criteria for participation; recommended continued study and support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support OED annual registration fee (with considerations for agents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC supports the annual registration fee in order to make certain that the roll of registered practitioners is up-to-date and to help defray the cost of operating the OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: annual fee aligns costs to beneficiaries; consider lower fees for agents who may be more burdened; ensure payment mechanisms are easy and that there is clarity on excusing late payments when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate CLE discount effectiveness and define qualifying CLE content/providers
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC supports the goal of improving the services provided by the patent bar to the public. However, it is not clear whether encouraging CLE will in fact bring about this desired result. More information supporting the effectiveness of such a CLE incentive would be helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: study whether CLE incentives improve practitioner services; define what content (technical vs legal) and providers qualify; consider whether non-lawyer patent agents should be eligible for CLE discounts and whether CLE should be required for them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fee proposals include aggregate expected revenue and linkage to improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO has not yet presented an aggregate expected revenue increase for the fee proposal. The PPAC notes the case for fee increases would be further bolstered with explanations of how additional revenue will support desired improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: provide transparent revenue projections and explicit links between funds raised and planned improvements (e.g., IT modernization, examiner hiring/training, operating reserve).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider alternatives or selective fee increases to achieve revenue targets
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternative would be selective further increases to filing and examination fees or maintenance fees to achieve the same projected revenue increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: USPTO should balance fee structure impacts on users; consider targeted adjustments rather than broad uniform increases where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and report FY statutory compliance and external perception survey results
rubrics_metrics.description: FY 2018 statutory compliance data shows strong compliance rates for allowances in all statutory compliance categories; compliance rates for 35 U.S.C. §101 strong for all office action types, but external perception survey reported only ~26% found §101 rejections 'reasonable' most of the time; §103 compliance down from FY2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: report and analyze statutory compliance by category (§101, §§102/103, §112); use external perception surveys to identify perception vs measured compliance gaps and address through guidance/training.
